data.name: Reshma
data.gender_notes: Reshma is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Reshma means soft, tender, gentle. It is a name that evokes a sense of warmth and nurturing. It is often used for girls born under the influence of the Moon, and is associated with the natural world and the cycles of life. The name Reshma carries the meaning “Soft, tender, gentle” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Reshma usually hope their child will grow to embody soft, tender, gentle and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Reshma is a name that carries deep spiritual significance. It is believed to represent the softer, more nurturing aspects of the divine. It is a name that inspires compassion, empathy, and a deep connection to the natural world.
data.etymology: Reshma belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Soft, tender, gentle.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Reshma total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Reshma is rooted in Indian cultural traditions, and is often used to describe a gentle, kind-hearted, and nurturing nature. It is a popular name for girls in the Indian subcontinent, and can be found across different regions and communities.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name Reshma is thought to reflect the divine qualities of compassion and nurturing. It is a reminder of the importance of cultivating a tender and gentle spirit, and of the power of love and care to transform and heal. Reshma is also associated with the goddesses of nurturing, such as Kamadhenu, the divine cow who offers sustenance, and Parvati, the consort of Shiva who personifies love, fertility, and nourishment.
